requirement:
The hash recorded for a selected tag MUST describe the source snapshot that
produced its delivered excerpt, even if the file changes before `finish_search`.
rationale:
**Obligation.** `requirements.authoring.finish_search.snapshot` says the hash recorded for a selected tag MUST describe the source snapshot that produced the delivered excerpt. That must hold even if the file changes before `finish_search`. A passing test therefore has to do three things. It has to deliver a search. It has to change the file afterwards. It has to show that `finish_search` still records the hash from delivery time, not a hash of the changed file.

**Main test.** `src/authoring/searches.rs#mod[tests]/fn[selected_dependencies_keep_the_delivered_hash_and_accumulate_without_reads]` is marked `{test}` for the subject and covers this case directly.
- It delivers a search (`search(..., "fn")`) over a file with `fn first` and `fn second`.
- It computes `original` with `outline_input` from the pre-mutation file.
- It then rewrites `fn first`, so its body changes and so does its structural hash.
- It calls `finish_search` with `used:["1","1"]` and asserts `finish.inputs == [original]`. That assertion enforces that the recorded hash is the delivery-time one and not a recomputed one.
- It calls `crate::evidence::validate_input` on the recorded input against the mutated file and asserts a "hash" error. That confirms the mutation really changed the hash and the recorded value is stale relative to the current file.
- It also finishes `fn[second]` after the mutation and checks the result against a fresh `outline_input`. `fn[second]` is unchanged, so this only confirms that it is recorded correctly. It does not exercise the snapshot rule.

**Second test.** `src/authoring/mod.rs#mod[tests]/fn[a_helper_used_only_through_a_search_snippet_invalidates_saved_evidence_when_weakened]` is also marked for the subject and serves the `helper_freshness` example. It finishes a search tag without any `habeas` read, then weakens the helper after finishing. It asserts that the recorded input for the helper carries a hash and that validation reports a hash mismatch. That is complementary evidence that the recorded hash is the real structural hash of the excerpted node. It does not mutate before finishing, so the main test above carries the "changes before `finish_search`" obligation.

**Implementation shape, used only to judge scenario coverage.** `src/authoring/searches.rs#impl[Searches]/fn[prepare]` captures the hash for every tag when the result is prepared, from the assessment's cached outline. `fn[finish]` only looks the stored input up. `ripgrep` and `ast_grep` both go through this one code path. The ripgrep scenario therefore stands in for both, and there is no separate distinction to test.

**Result.** I found no gap. The requirement has one obligation and its mutate-before-finish scenario is tested with assertions that would fail if finish recomputed the hash. No acknowledgments (`{fixme}`) apply.

text: The hash recorded for a selected tag MUST describe the source snapshot that
produced its delivered excerpt, even if the file changes before `finish_search`.
A marked test calls `assert_refusal`. A search excerpt of that helper supplies
the refusal and byte-preservation assertions used to justify the judgment.
The model finishes the search with the helper's tag without reading it with
`habeas`. Saved evidence MUST include the helper's outline input.
Replacing the helper with a no-op MUST make that evidence stale, even when
the marked test source is unchanged.
